> **Legacy document.** This template drives `catcheR_10Xcatch()`, the original
> entry point that runs the bundled shell scripts through `system()` and writes
> its intermediates into the input folder. It is kept for reference and has
> **not** been executed on a real dataset. For new 10x analyses use
> `catcheR_tenxcatch_analysis_EB.Rmd`, which runs natively in R and writes only
> into `Output/`, and has been knitted end to end on AB019a with the 0.4.0
> code (15.3 min, 60 files). See `docs/pipeline-10x.md`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
library(catcheR); library(knitr)
SCRATCH <- file.path(params$analysis_dir, params$scratch)
OUT     <- file.path(params$analysis_dir, params$output)
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
show <- function(f, ext = "jpg") {
  p <- file.path(SCRATCH, paste0(f, ".", ext))
  if (file.exists(p)) knitr::include_graphics(p) else invisible(NULL)
}
```

# How this path differs from the other two

`catcheR_10Xcatch()` is the original CATCHER pipeline. Unlike
[catcheR_pipcatch()] and [catcheR_parsecatch()], which are pure R, it drives
bundled shell and R scripts, so it needs a working `bash` and writes its
intermediates **into the input folder** rather than into `Output/`. The folder
convention below therefore puts `scratch/` where the pipeline expects to work.

Three further differences worth knowing before you compare results across
chemistries:

| | 10X | PIPseq | Parse |
|---|---|---|---|
| cassette read | read 2 | read 2 | **read 1** |
| cell barcode | read 1, fixed 16 nt slice | read 1, 4 tiers with phasing | read 2, 3 ligation rounds |
| molecular index | 12 nt UMI | 3 nt, not deduplicable | 10 nt UMI |
| default `ratio` | 5 | 2 | 2 |

# Inputs

`catcheR_10Xcatch()` requires `rc_barcodes_genes.csv` under exactly that name
in the same folder; it is not a parameter.

```{r inputs}
need <- c(params$fastq_r1, params$fastq_r2, "rc_barcodes_genes.csv")
inv <- data.frame(file = need, exists = file.exists(file.path(SCRATCH, need)))
inv <- rbind(inv, data.frame(file = params$expression_matrix,
                             exists = file.exists(file.path(SCRATCH, params$expression_matrix))))
stopifnot(all(inv$exists))
kable(inv, caption = sprintf("Inputs found in %s", SCRATCH))
```

# Extraction and QC

```{r tenx, cache=TRUE}
catcheR_10Xcatch(folder            = SCRATCH,
                 fastq.read1       = params$fastq_r1,
                 fastq.read2       = params$fastq_r2,
                 expression.matrix = params$expression_matrix,
                 reference         = params$reference,
                 UCI.length        = params$uci_length,
                 threads           = params$threads,
                 percentage        = params$percentage,
                 mode              = params$mode,
                 ratio             = params$ratio,
                 samples           = params$samples,
                 x                 = params$zoom_x,
                 y                 = params$zoom_y)
```

# Cell filtering and unperturbed cells

```{r downstream, cache=TRUE}
catcheR_filtercatch(folder = SCRATCH, percentage = params$percentage,
                    ratio = params$ratio, samples = params$samples)
catcheR_nocatch(folder = SCRATCH, samples = params$samples)
```

# The thirteen plots

```{r plots, fig.show="hold", out.width="48%"}
for (f in c("barcode_distribution", "gene_distribution", "UMIxUCI", "UCIxcell",
            "percentage_of_UMIxUCI_dist", "2D_percentage_of_UMIxUCI_UMI_count",
            "2D_percentage_of_UMIxUCI_UMI_count_thresholds", "true_UCIxcell",
            "2D_percentage_of_UMIxUCI_UMI_count_trueorfalse", "cellsxclone",
            "cellsxclone_log10", "2D_percentage_of_UMIxUCI_UMI_count_ValidCells")) show(f)
show(sprintf("UMIxUCI_%s_%s", params$zoom_x, params$zoom_y))
```

# Files written

```{r manifest}
f <- list.files(SCRATCH, pattern = "\\.(csv|jpg|pdf|txt)$")
kable(data.frame(file = f,
                 size_KB = round(file.size(file.path(SCRATCH, f)) / 1024, 1)),
      caption = sprintf("Outputs in %s", SCRATCH))
```
